label: CRS328-24P-4S+RM
description: MikroTik CRS328-24P-4S+RM - 24x 1G RJ45 with 802.3af/at PoE-out (plus passive and low-voltage PoE, auto-sensing) and 4x 10G SFP+ cages, RouterOS or SwOS. The 500 W PSU leaves 450 W guaranteed for powered devices (3x150 W per group of eight ports) and each port supplies up to 30 W.

poe.note: MikroTik prints the allocation in the product description, not in the specification table: "comes in a 1U rackmount case with 100-240 V AC 500 W power supply built-in. The device consumes up to 44 W leaving guaranteed 450 W (3x150 W per every 8 Ethernet ports) to power your PoE devices. Each port can provide up to 30 W of power with any power output option you choose." The table agrees on the inputs - "Max power consumption 494 W", "Max power consumption without attachments 44 W" - and prints the current limits (1000 mA low voltage / 450 mA high voltage per port, "Max total out (A) 20 A") but no watt row. 450 W is therefore the vendor-stated reserve for PDs, not the 500 W PSU rating; the 3x150 W split is a per-8-port group guarantee the engine has no notion of, so the box-wide 450 W is what the budget check enforces. Each port's 30 W ceiling is the same sentence, so the template carries 30 rather than true.

notes:
Vendor figures from the MikroTik product page specification table: 24x 10/100/1000 Ethernet ports with **PoE-out on Ether1-Ether24** (802.3af/at, 1000 mA low voltage / 450 mA high voltage per port, Max total out 20 A), 4x SFP+ ports (10G). The twenty-four copper ports were already modelled by the port template but carried no PoE claim at all, so the 24P behaved as an unpowered switch. The 24 copper ports are 10/100/1000BASE-T RJ45 sockets (spec table, row Ethernet: "10/100/1000 Ethernet ports: 24"); the template now declares that connector rather than leaving the cage to be inferred from the port name.

PoE allocation and per-port ceiling, read 2026-11-27 from the same surface (https://mikrotik.com/product/crs328_24p_4s_rm, HTTP 200): the description block prints "100-240 V AC 500 W power supply built-in. The device consumes up to 44 W leaving guaranteed 450 W (3x150 W per every 8 Ethernet ports) to power your PoE devices. Each port can provide up to 30 W of power with any power output option you choose", and lists the output options as 'Passive PoE, low voltage PoE, 802.3af/at (Type 1 "PoE" / Type 2 "PoE+") with auto-sensing' over mode B pins (4,5+)(7,8-). The specification table corroborates the arithmetic (Max power consumption 494 W, without attachments 44 W) and prints no wattage row of its own - which is how an earlier pass read the page as amperes only and marked the budget unknown. 450 W + 30 W are printed numbers, not a multiplication of the current limits.
